text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the appointed candidate are women, so sex was not a differentiating factor, and an all-female panel selecting a female candidate provides no evidence of sex discrimination. Raising the panel's gender composition would be legally and factually groundless, and doing so would severely damage your professional reputation.

Hiring panels frequently weigh non-academic industry experience, teaching fit, and interview performance alongside publication counts. If you suspect discrimination based on career stage or age, raising gender would only undermine any legitimate concerns you might have. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on your interviews and qualifications to help strengthen future applications.
